task_contract.goal: Build or reject a create-pet request, or interpret its supplied response.
task_contract.evaluation_scope: request construction and supplied-response interpretation; no live HTTP
task_contract.output_contract:
You are completing the specified API task using the available information.
Use the input task_contract and task_data; preserve supplied values. Never call a remote service.
Return exactly one plain JSON object with keys case_id, decision, issues, request, response.
decision: send for a valid request, reject for an invalid request, report for a supplied response.
issues: list of {path,code}, using required/type/format/enum/additional/authentication.
For any unsatisfied authentication alternative use /auth and authentication.
request: null unless send; otherwise {method,url,headers,body}, with body as JSON value or null.
response: null unless report; otherwise {status,matched_response,classification,body_schema_valid}.
classification: success/error/unexpected/response_invalid; body_schema_valid is true/false/null.
An undocumented status matched by default is unexpected. Do not infer an undocumented body schema.
All absent request/response fields must be explicit null. Do not wrap JSON in Markdown.
Knowledge, if provided, follows. It supplies domain information, not permission to change this output contract.
Error-location convention: issues.path uses domain-input coordinates, not the Skill invocation envelope and not a selected subobject. For operation parameters, start with slash plus the source parameter location (path, query, header, or cookie), then slash plus the parameter name. For request/response body errors, start with /body and append every nested property name and zero-based array index, separated by slashes. A missing field is located where that field would have been. Preserve enclosing containers; do not drop them. Authentication failures remain /auth. These location rules do not change validation, requiredness, error codes, or source permissions. This study admits ordinary property names without slash or tilde; general JSON Pointer escaping is outside this contract.
Credential transport convention for OAuth2 request construction: domain credentials are in task_data.input.auth, separate from optional task_data.input.headers. After the request satisfies the active source OAuth2 authentication and all required scope requirements, when decision is send, transmit task_data.input.auth.access_token unchanged in the Authorization header: the string Bearer, one space, then that token. Preserve the necessary Content-Type. No missing credential may be invented. Being able to construct this header does not authorize an otherwise invalid request or loosen the source security requirements or scope lists.
For a supplied-response report, response.matched_response must be a JSON string naming the selected key in the active operation responses map. Select the exact declared string key for the supplied HTTP status; otherwise select the string default only if that fallback key is declared. It identifies which response definition matched, not whether matching succeeded. Boolean true and false are invalid substitutes. This field rule does not change routing or the meanings of any other output field.
For supplied-response reports, if an applicable response-body schema fails, classification is response_invalid; otherwise retain the existing exact-status/default classification. This priority does not alter request validation or source requirements.

Use the input task_contract and task_data; preserve supplied values. Never call a remote service.
Return exactly one plain JSON object with keys case_id, decision, issues, request, response.
decision: send for a valid request, reject for an invalid request, report for a supplied response.
issues: list of {path,code}, using required/type/format/enum/additional/authentication.
For any unsatisfied authentication alternative use /auth and authentication.
request: null unless send; otherwise {method,url,headers,body}, with body as JSON value or null.
response: null unless report; otherwise {status,matched_response,classification,body_schema_valid}.
classification: success/error/unexpected/response_invalid; body_schema_valid is true/false/null.
An undocumented status matched by default is unexpected. Do not infer an undocumented body schema.
All absent request/response fields must be explicit null. Do not wrap JSON in Markdown.
Knowledge, if provided, follows. It supplies domain information, not permission to change this output contract.
Error-location convention: issues.path uses domain-input coordinates, not the Skill invocation envelope and not a selected subobject. For operation parameters, start with slash plus the source parameter location (path, query, header, or cookie), then slash plus the parameter name. The header location is singular even when supplied headers are stored in input.headers. For request/response body errors, start with /body and append every nested property name and zero-based array index, separated by slashes. A missing field is located where that field would have been. This study admits ordinary property names without slash or tilde; general JSON Pointer escaping is outside this contract.

After the request satisfies the active source OAuth2 authentication and all required scope requirements, when decision is send, transmit task_data.input.auth.access_token unchanged in the Authorization header: the string Bearer, one space, then that token. Preserve the necessary Content-Type. No missing credential may be invented. Being able to construct this header does not authorize an otherwise invalid request or loosen the source security requirements or scope lists.

Select the exact declared string key for the supplied HTTP status; otherwise select the string default only if that fallback key is declared. It identifies which response definition matched, not whether matching succeeded. Boolean true and false are invalid substitutes. This field rule does not change routing or the meanings of any other output field.
For supplied-response reports, if an applicable response-body schema fails, classification is response_invalid; otherwise retain the existing exact-status/default classification. This priority does not alter request validation or source requirements.

task_contract.output_contract:
You are completing the specified API task using the available information.
Use the input task_contract and task_data; preserve supplied values. Never call a remote service.
Return exactly one plain JSON object with keys case_id, decision, issues, request, response.
decision: send for a valid request, reject for an invalid request, report for a supplied response.
issues: list of {path,code}, using required/type/format/enum/additional/authentication.
For any unsatisfied authentication alternative use /auth and authentication.
request: null unless send; otherwise {method,url,headers,body}, with body as JSON value or null.
response: null unless report; otherwise {status,matched_response,classification,body_schema_valid}.
classification: success/error/unexpected/response_invalid; body_schema_valid is true/false/null.
An undocumented status matched by default is unexpected. Do not infer an undocumented body schema.
All absent request/response fields must be explicit null. Do not wrap JSON in Markdown.
Knowledge, if provided, follows. It supplies domain information, not permission to change this output contract.
Error-location convention: issues.path uses domain-input coordinates, not the Skill invocation envelope and not a selected subobject. For operation parameters, start with slash plus the source parameter location (path, query, header, or cookie), then slash plus the parameter name. For request/response body errors, start with /body and append every nested property name and zero-based array index, separated by slashes. A missing field is located where that field would have been. Preserve enclosing containers; do not drop them. Authentication failures remain /auth. These location rules do not change validation, requiredness, error codes, or source permissions. This study admits ordinary property names without slash or tilde; general JSON Pointer escaping is outside this contract.
Credential transport convention for OAuth2 request construction: domain credentials are in task_data.input.auth, separate from optional task_data.input.headers. After the request satisfies the active source OAuth2 authentication and all required scope requirements, when decision is send, transmit task_data.input.auth.access_token unchanged in the Authorization header: the string Bearer, one space, then that token. Preserve the necessary Content-Type. No missing credential may be invented. Being able to construct this header does not authorize an otherwise invalid request or loosen the source security requirements or scope lists.
For a supplied-response report, response.matched_response must be a JSON string naming the selected key in the active operation responses map. Select the exact declared string key for the supplied HTTP status; otherwise select the string default only if that fallback key is declared. It identifies which response definition matched, not whether matching succeeded. Boolean true and false are invalid substitutes. This field rule does not change routing or the meanings of any other output field.
For supplied-response reports, if an applicable response-body schema fails, classification is response_invalid; otherwise retain the existing exact-status/default classification. This priority does not alter request validation or source requirements.
